title: Supervise the whole native lifecycle outside the child
environment: Tested Python/Windows supervision. No hard-real-time OS guarantee or general native-SDK defect is asserted; terminate only the owned child.
goal: Finish a short native-SDK observation and report its outcome within a bound.
approach: Historical failed assumption: The observation-loop deadline was assumed to cover native initialization and teardown, and final-only output was assumed sufficient.
what_worked: Historical correction: Use parent-owned child-process supervision with a total deadline and cleanup reserve, bounded intermediate aggregates and pre-close evidence. Record both result and actual child exit. Verification reported by the source: Spawned import/constructor/open/close/exit-hang controls and partial-IPC tests passed. A later live recovery exited normally in about 20.25 seconds with 1,200 valid callbacks; this did not retrospectively identify the original hang.
what_failed: Historical observed failure: A nominal twenty-second probe was still alive after 43.1 seconds with no final aggregate; forced stop left stage/activity uncertain.
why: Confirmed containment gap: synchronous lifecycle calls lay outside the loop deadline. The historical stalled stage and underlying native cause remained unknown.
improved_method: Bound the complete lifecycle externally and retain partial evidence. Missing summary means unknown activity; a pre-close result does not prove cleanup completed.
when_to_use: Tested Python/Windows supervision. No hard-real-time OS guarantee or general native-SDK defect is asserted; terminate only the owned child.
when_not_to_use: No hard-real-time OS guarantee or general native-SDK defect is asserted; terminate only the owned child.
known_limitations: This is an independently curated generalization of an earlier recorded failure. No source-side experiment was rerun during this registration; observation_date is the 2026-10-09 knowledge-review date, not the incident date. Applicability and root-cause claims remain limited to the source-reported conditions.
